claim: Forgetting patterns in LLM post-training vary across model families but show little consistent dependence on model size and are not inherently domain-driven.
falsifier: For a set of LLMs from different families and sizes, apply the same post-training procedure and measure forgetting across multiple domains; the claim predicts that forgetting patterns will differ by family but not systematically by size or domain.

conditions: Post-training applied to already aligned models
Evaluation using CapTrack framework across multiple model families, domains, and algorithms
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported model families, domains, and post-training algorithms; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Model family, model size–Forgetting patterns principle

claim: Product aggregation of per-step confidence scores for fault detection in LLM agents can be confounded by trajectory length, producing high ROC-AUC even when confidence signals are uninformative (e.g., replaced by random or length-based surrogates).
falsifier: On a new benchmark, compare product-aggregation ROC-AUC using real confidence scores vs. random or length-based surrogates; if surrogates match or exceed real scores, product aggregation is confounded by trajectory length.

conditions: Replacing real confidences with i.i.d. U(0,1) draws or deterministic 1/length values matches or exceeds real-product ROC-AUC for nearly every method
The lone exception is random surrogate under UAM
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the ALFWorld benchmark and the specific methods (ReAct+UE, UAM, proposed decomposition); the confounding effect may not generalize to other benchmarks or aggregation methods.

title: Product aggregation of per-step–Fault-detection ROC-AUC principle
